transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-03-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE); Sofia Marquez (Redwood CSM); Carlos Jimenez (MercuryFleet VP Eng); Aisha Khan (Head of ML); Ben Wallace (Platform Lead); Ellen Park (Sec Arch)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
We walked through deployment options — hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC; network peering nuances, SLOs and cost trade-offs; security checklist requested. Action items noted.

Topics:
- VPC and peering
- SLO targets and tail latency
- Data residency and retention
- Pilot scope
- Security artifacts and KMS

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um we wanted to run through the onboarding orientation for MercuryFleet and make sure we capture SLOs, networking, and security needs. Quick intros — Liam from infra and me AE.
[00:28] Carlos Jimenez: Hey, Carlos here. Sorry for the slight delay, had a back-to-back. We're excited to get this moving. Primary goals are predictable latency for tracking agents, and costs need to stay under our current budget envelopes.
[00:45] Liam O'Connor: Great. Quick note on our side — we typically recommend a short smoke bench first, like a baseline run with 10k requests to see distribution. We'll use Redwood's hosted for the pilot unless you need a private VPC.
[01:10] Aisha Khan: For the workloads, most sequences average 120 tokens but we have occasional 1k token outliers when we do full route summarization. That affects KV cache and batching, right?
[01:30] Liam O'Connor: Yeah, the long-tail is important. We can configure auto-batching thresholds and prefix caching, and we also have recommendations for quantized variants to save cost on less sensitive routes.
[01:50] Ben Wallace: On network — we need egress control. The security team wants to avoid public internet egress for PII traffic. Is the private deployment the only way to guarantee that?
[02:10] Maya Patel: Not necessarily. For MercuryFleet we can do private VPC peering so traffic stays in your cloud VPC to Redwood's private endpoints. Or run our Private on-prem package if you need zero egress.
[02:35] Ellen Park: If we peer, we still need KMS integration and audit logs shipped to our SIEM. Do you have HSM-compatible flows? And does Redwood preserve audit log granularity for token-level tracing?
[02:55] Liam O'Connor: We support KMS integrations and can surface request-level trace IDs to your SIEM. HSM-backed key wraps are supported via our Private offering; hosted also integrates with major KMS providers but with different key custody models.
[03:20] Carlos Jimenez: Timeline — we want a pilot in two weeks, with an objective to go to a production A/B in six weeks if numbers look good. Success criteria: p99 latency under 650ms for the 95% of calls and end-to-end cost per 1k tokens under $X (we'll share exact target).
[03:45] Maya Patel: Sounds reasonable. We'll send a baseline plan and sample prompts to run. Liam will instrument the benchmark harness.
[04:05] Aisha Khan: Also SOC2 — we need SOC2 Type II artifacts and the standard penetration test reports. Can Redwood share those? And SAML SSO for team access.
[04:25] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll share the security packet with SOC2, pen test summaries, incident response playbook and our SAML SSO setup docs. I'll include contact for the security eng folks.
[04:45] Ben Wallace: On the infra spec — if we scale to dedicated, what GPU types do you usually recommend for throughput? We saw some reference to A10G and H100s; curious about cost/latency tradeoffs.
[05:05] Liam O'Connor: For throughput-dense reranking we often recommend higher-memory GPUs like H100s; A10G is good for balanced workloads. We can surface model-specific performance profiles once we have your sample workload.
[05:30] Carlos Jimenez: Any requirement for data residency? We have EU customers and need logs to remain in eu-west-1 for regulatory reasons for some datasets.
[05:48] Maya Patel: We can pin model variants to region and ensure data handling occurs in chosen region when on Hosted with region selection or with Private deployments.
[06:05] An aside where transcript picks up with crosstalk and some misrecognition...
[06:20] Liam O'Connor: Ok, next steps from Redwood: I'll draft the benchmark plan, Maya will send security docs, and we'll propose pilot start windows. Also we can run a quick throughput test to show latency impact with batching config changes.
[06:45] Carlos Jimenez: Great. We'll share a sample dataset and an infra diagram for the team's firewall rules and egress policies.
[07:00] Aisha Khan: One more question — what's the default token retention? We want short retention for PII, but need embeddings persisted for feature store for 90 days.
[07:20] Sofia Marquez: On retention we offer customer-configurable retention windows; we can set retention per-route. For embeddings persisting we can integrate with your object store or Redwood-managed retention — both options possible.
[07:45] Ben Wallace: For SSO, do you do SCIM provisioning?
[08:00] Maya Patel: Yep, SCIM and SAML supported. We'll include setup steps in the packet.
[08:12] Ellen Park: Competitor question — we've talked to AltServe AI, they pushed aggressive pricing but limited region support. Any differences to call out?
[08:30] Maya Patel: Our differentiation is the unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and the observability with token-level cost breakdowns; we'll show you the dashboards during the pilot.
[08:50] Closing recap
Maya Patel: Recap — Redwood action: send security packet (SOC2, pen test), draft benchmark test plan, propose pilot start dates. MercuryFleet action: share sample prompts/workloads, infra diagram, confirm budget SLO targets. Follow-up security deep dive scheduled for 2027-03-09 10:00 PT.
[09:30] Meeting ends
